title.value: Monitor open GitHub pull requests with a self-healing agent

introduction.value: An OpenClaw agent watches 26+ pull requests across several repos, with a cron scanner every 5 minutes and alerts pushed to the author; it caught one of its own critical bugs.

method.value: A Python script using the gh CLI runs from cron every 5 minutes. It compares each tracked PR with a saved JSON snapshot and writes important changes to a pending-alerts file. A separate watchdog script runs every 30 minutes. The OpenClaw agent wakes on a heartbeat, runs the watchdog, and pushes undelivered alerts through Feishu.

outcome.value: It tracks 26 PRs: 1 merged, 1 closed, 24 open. The watchdog exposed an older v2 script that had crashed on its first run and never worked in 18 days.

notes.value: Alerts sit in a flat JSON file, so if the agent misses a heartbeat they can be lost. The author would use a queue and webhooks instead.

source_text.body:
Monitor open GitHub pull requests with a self-healing agent
An OpenClaw agent watches 26+ pull requests across several repos, with a cron scanner every 5 minutes and alerts pushed to the author; it caught one of its own critical bugs.
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
A Python script using the gh CLI runs from cron every 5 minutes. It compares each tracked PR with a saved JSON snapshot and writes important changes to a pending-alerts file. A separate watchdog script runs every 30 minutes. The OpenClaw agent wakes on a heartbeat, runs the watchdog, and pushes undelivered alerts through Feishu.
How it went
It tracks 26 PRs: 1 merged, 1 closed, 24 open. The watchdog exposed an older v2 script that had crashed on its first run and never worked in 18 days.
Worth knowing
Alerts sit in a flat JSON file, so if the agent misses a heartbeat they can be lost. The author would use a queue and webhooks instead.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Watch my open GitHub pull requests across these repos: [repo list]. Every 5 minutes check for new review comments, failing CI checks, merge conflicts, or merges, and message me on [Telegram/other chat] only when something needs my attention, with a link and one line on what changed. Do not push commits, comment, or merge anything without showing me first.
Original source: https://dev.to/armorbreak/i-built-a-self-healing-pr-monitor-with-openclaw-and-it-caught-its-own-bugs-41e8
